trickyParts: The merge of main forced two judgements. The daemon API contract: both sides added an entry numbered 44, and main's is released, so this change takes 45 and every mirror moves with it. A turn the daemon cuts: main deleted Quiesce outright, so answerByTurnEnd's m.interrupt guard had nothing left to read and went, with the test whose subject it was; that test's surviving assertion, that a refused answer takes the ask's clock back, is now in the unseen-turn test.

main also made settle wait for prompt_result, so at a turn's end the task can still be in the worker's hands. What the machine holds for the turn — the round's end and the stale-plugin relaunch — therefore runs from afterTurn, called by turnEnded when no result is outstanding and by promptResulted otherwise. Without it the round's end told the worker nothing (it still held a pending task) and the relaunch took an unretired task back.

The round's end is held in memory (Machine.roundOver) rather than left to the next sweep, which is the architect's line for a working worker: released when its turn ends, not a minute later. letGo drops it with the process, and the sweep still posts the end again for a round that is open, so a restart that forgets the mark loses nothing.

A role's own PostgreSQL is legion-testpg with LEGION_TESTPG_DIR under the issue's volume and a port of the role's own. Its role is NOSUPERUSER, so internal/daemon's outbox tests, which drop their temporary database with FORCE, fail intermittently with 'permission denied to terminate process'; `grant pg_signal_backend to legion_test`, run as the bootstrap superuser over the cluster's own unix socket under <LEGION_TESTPG_DIR>/sockets, ends it. This round's server was port 5447.
The pod was replaced mid-round at 03:02Z. Everything survived because the work was committed and pushed to legion/INFRA-484-wip at each step; the two Postgres servers did not, and were rebuilt.
deviations: The architect's line 1 says 'key the carry-on task by round id'. The key that decides whether the task is sent is PodUpdateEnded.Replaced, since the round's id cannot say what became of its pod; the round id is carried too and decides whether the end applies at all. Both are on the event, and the reviewer's own prescription is the Replaced flag.
discoveredComplexity: A test of this branch was already red at the branch head before the merge, introduced by this round's own unseenTurn mark: TestPodUpdateTakesTheTurnsEndAsTheAnswerOfAClaimBelowTheContract started its turn with a StreamTurnStart naming no delivery, which is exactly the shape the new mark refuses. The turn the test's prose describes is the one the round's own ask started, so the start now names that ask's delivery id and no assertion was weakened. It is recorded here because a round's own new rule turning one of its earlier tests red is the kind of thing a full-package run catches and a targeted one does not.
